And in this same year, al-Malik al-Mu'azzam, the lord of Damascus, went forth,
and plundered the territory of Hama.
And al-Malik al-Ashraf, his brother, heard [of it],
and sent to accuse him on this account.
He, however, having become offended with him,
sent to his other brother, Shihab al-Din Ghazi,
who was then the lord of Khilat and of Mayyafariqin,
and caused him to rebel against al-Ashraf.
And al-Ashraf went forth and marched against Khilat,
and took it from his brother in battle.
And when he captured his brother, he did not kill him,
but left Mayyafariqin to him and sent him thither.
At this same time, the Baron Constantine the Regent (Pail) sent to Mar Ignatius, our Patriarch,
and to Mar Constantine, the Catholicos of the Armenians,
[bidding them go] to the daughter of King Leo,
so that she might come down from Seleucia and be pacified,
in order that they might make an arrangement profitable to the Christian community;
because on account of the schism,
behold, Sultan 'Ala al-Din, the lord of the land of the Romans, had seized most of the fortresses of Cilicia.
And those blessed men went,
and although they pleaded with her much and admonished her,
she did not yield to their persuasion.
And she even blamed them,
and called them companions of a murderer and of a shedder of innocent blood (and murderers and shedders of blood).
And they were unable to bring about any relief for her,
but left her and came away like men who had accomplished nothing.
Then that Regent went thither in person,
and demanded of the Franks (Hospitallers) that they should deliver her to him by force.
And they replied:
"Our houses and villages are walled cities of refuge for Christians,
and we are not able to surrender a woman, a queen, who has taken refuge with us."
Then that Regent devised a stratagem,
and bought from them with gold the fortress and everything in it,
and cast them out of it,
and he became its lord and ruler.
And he took the queen by her arm,
and dragged her and brought her down by force to Tarsus.
And he assembled the Patriarchs, bishops, and priests,
and they crowned her together with his son Hethum (Othon).
And Hethum was proclaimed king of Cilicia on the Sunday of Pentecost,
the fourteenth of Haziran,
the year one thousand five hundred and thirty-seven of the Greeks (1226 of our Lord).
